title: Phoretic colloids on a closed particle ledger (SID): from a uniform random gas, Janus composites grow on food and divide when a B band forms between two A bodies that both flee it; generation 7-10 by particle identity in 800 t on 2 seeds, labkit generation 4 vs 0-1 with turnover off
summary: world.py: the phoretic Janus world (20261026T0254-c33-phoretic-janus-claim; A makes c1, B makes c2, mu [[1,-1],[1,0.5]]: B sticks to A bodies, A flees B) plus a closed particle ledger: inert food particles F (900, faster diffusion) become A at kA=0.05 per A neighbour within r=2 (A autocatalytic), become B at kB=0.2 per B neighbour (needs an A neighbour), and A and B decay back to F at 0.01 and 0.02. From a uniform random mix (700 A, 200 B, 900 F) A and B settle at about 1040 and 240. Composites grow, and when one carries B between two A lobes both lobes run from it, the B band stretches and the body separates into two composites that each keep B (deep_splits_seed0.png, deep_splits_seed1.png: all 8 randomly chosen splits at generation >= 5-8). Particle-identity lineage (lineage.py; a split is persistent when both children live >= 20 t and never share a cluster again; merge-aware generations), t=800: seed 0, 129 splits, 190 merges, 63 persistent, max generation 10; seed 1, 126 / 184 / 55, generation 7; 61/63 and 52/55 persistent splits leave B in both daughters. labkit packs (tpack, seeds 0 and 1, t=400): 11 and 12 persistent splits, max generation 4, merge/split 1.67 and 1.23. Matched twin with turnover off at the steady-state particle counts (1300 A, 250 B, 250 inert F; tpack_off, same seeds, grid and duration): labkit 0 and 1 persistent splits, generation 0 and 1; particle lineage at t=400, seed 0: 1 persistent split vs 23 (generation 1 vs 5).

claims.statement: From a uniform random particle mix (seeds 0 and 1), A-B composites condense, grow on the food ledger and divide by the same route, a B band between two A lobes that both flee it, into two composites that each carry B, repeatedly: generation 7-10 by particle identity in 800 t and generation 4 by labkit in 400 t; with turnover off at the same particle counts there is at most one persistent split and generation 0-1.
claims.track: seed 1, the generation-5 split at t=566 (deep_splits_seed1.png row 3): a 123-particle composite with a B band between two A lobes separates into 67 + 55, both keeping B, and both persist

controls_run.D: tpack_off/ (WORLD_P {"NA":1300,"NB":250,"NF":250,"kA":0,"kB":0,"dA":0,"dB":0}: no turnover at the steady-state counts, seeds 0 and 1, t=400): labkit 0/1 persistent splits, generation 0/1; lineage_particles.txt last two lines (seed 0, t=400): 1 persistent split, generation 1 without turnover vs 23, generation 5 with it

limits: Reticulate: merges outnumber splits (190 vs 129, 184 vs 126 by particle identity; labkit merge/split 1.2-1.7), so confidence is capped at medium; generations are counted through merges by the largest parent. Daughters are often unequal (median 39-44 vs 73-80 particles). Matter is made only from food and decays back (a designed ledger), so E is not claimed; the reaction rules are proximity catalysis, not a division rule. Motility: 13 of 63 and 17 of 55 dividing parents had travelled >= 3 cluster diameters since their own birth (track364_seed0.png shows one), but the swim-then-divide strip is not clean enough to claim M on the same individuals. One parameter point, 2 seeds; no dt/2 or box-size test for this variant (the Janus world's dt/2 is in the parent claim).
